newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel visit aims to put China ties back on track.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel visit aims to put China ties back on track.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel departs on Sunday for China, aiming to put ties with Beijing firmly back on track after a row over Tibet earlier this year caused the postponement of the visit.
Foreign ministry officials said Kinkel would meet his Chinese counterpart Qian Qichen, President Jiang Zemin, Prime Minister Li Peng during the five-day trip.

Talks were likely to concentrate on how the two countries could co-operate more closely in the future, matters of environmental policy and preparation for a state visit by President Roman Herzog scheduled for next month.

Kinkel had originally planned to visit China in July but Beijing withdrew his invitation after the German lower house of parliament passed a resolution accusing China of trying to eradicate Tibet's cultural identity.

After a meeting on the sidelines of the United Nations general assembly in September, Kinkel and Qian said they had cleared up any problems between China and its biggest European trade partner, and Kinkel's invitation was renewed.

Relatives and supporters of dissidents held in Chinese custody have urged Kinkel to raise the issue on his trip. Asked if Kinkel would also meet dissidents, ministry officials said the exact schedule had not yet been decided.
German foreign ministry spokesman Martin Erdmann said Kinkel and Qian had agreed human rights issues would continue to be discussed between the two sides despite their differcences.
Erdmann said the ministers had agreed "this dialogue should take place in a spirit of mutual respect and equality and not in a spirit of confrontation".

German opposition politicians have long been critical of Kinkel's policy towards China, accusing him of treading too softly on human rights issues for the sake of securing large industrial orders for German companies.

A delegation of around 20 represenatatives from German industry, many of them from companies specialising in technology which helps to protect the environment, are slated to accompany the foreign minister.
Officials said environmental policy was expected to be one of the main themes of the visit, with Kinkel opening a joint German-Chinese workshop on environmental issues on Monday.

As one of the world's leading exponents of environmental technology after the United States, Bonn is hoping German firms can cash in on the need for environmental protection measures in China's rapidly-growing economy.
Kinkel was also scheduled to inaugurate a new German embassy building in Beijing and visit the city of Chengdu, capital of the western province of Sichuan.
